October 2025
How we’re 
creating greater

Picture by Tony Gavin

The Chief Executive’s Report is presented to elected members at each SDCC monthly 
meeting. It forms a key part of our governance and oversight framework, supporting members 
in their role by providing timely updates on the work of the Council.
In line with Section 136(2) of the Local Government Act 2001 (as amended by the Local 
Government Reform Act 2014), the report outlines the performance of executive functions, 
the implementation of Council policy, and the delivery of services across the organisation.
This report should be read alongside updates provided to Area Committee Meetings and the 
quarterly Capital Progress Report, which together offer a comprehensive view of Council 
activity and progress.
Each edition includes:
•	Updates on how we are delivering on our Corporate Plan goals
•	Highlights of major initiatives and events
•	A visual snapshot of recent community and Council activities
The report also provides an opportunity to shine a light on areas of our work that may not 
always be in the spotlight but are vital to the day-to-day life of the county.

Climate Leadership
Community Climate Action Funding Reopens
Applications for funding under the 
Community Climate Action Programme 
reopen on 28 October this year. The 
€1.073 million fund supports not-for-
profit community organisations to deliver 
meaningful climate action with real local 
impact. 
The maximum funding available for a 
single project is €100,000. Previous 
projects have created warmer community 
spaces, installed solar power, reduced 
food waste and developed green spaces 
that help communities adapt to climate 
change. Organisations interested in 
applying or discussing project ideas 
are encouraged to get in touch at 
climatechange@sdublincoco.ie.
Liffey Valley to City Centre Core Bus Corridor 
The National Transport Authority has 
signed a contract with GMC Group Ltd. 
for the detailed design and construction 
of a nine point two kilometre Core Bus 
Corridor from Liffey Valley to the city 
centre as part of Bus Connects. 
The corridor will begin at Fonthill Road 
and connect with the new Liffey Valley 
Shopping Centre bus interchange, 
continuing to the city centre through 
Ballyfermot Village. 
This project is expected to improve the 
reliability and speed of bus services along 
the route, offering better sustainable 
travel options in South Dublin and 
supporting Ireland’s climate action 
commitments. 
The corridor will also feature 13.3 
kilometres of improved cycling and 
pedestrian infrastructure in both 
directions, making it easier and safer for 
people to choose active travel.
This scheme represents an important 
investment in sustainable travel for 
the county. Construction works on the 
sections in South Dublin are scheduled to 
begin in the fourth quarter of this year.

Quality Housing
Social and Affordable Homes Planned for Rathfarnham
With the support of the Housing Agency, 
we have acquired a key site at Stocking 
Avenue, Rathfarnham, Dublin 16. 
This acquisition, under the Government’s 
Housing for All Land Acquisition Fund 
overseen by the Housing Agency, marks 
a significant step in our continued 
commitment to delivering high-quality 
social and affordable housing across the 
county.
The site was approved for social and 
affordable funding at an initial cost of 
€8.25 million to acquire the land, with an 
estimated delivery of more than 240 new 
homes and a community facility upon it’s 
completion.
The development will be delivered as a 
mixed-tenure scheme, supporting the 
creation of inclusive and sustainable 
communities in line with national housing 
policy. It also forms part of the broader 
Housing Delivery Action Plan.
We are masterplan is being developed to 
maximise the potential of this site and 
adjoining lands in the council’s ownership. 
Proposals will be brought for review to 
the elected members in the first quarter 
of next year.
Innovative Modular Homes Proposed
Innovative modular homeless housing 
proposals are gaining traction as a 
sustainable and efficient solution to 
the growing issue of homelessness. 
This proposal forms part of the Dublin 
Regional Homeless Plan 2025/28, which 
aims to reduce reliance on the private 
sector for emergency accommodation.
The project involves developing a pilot 
modular housing scheme to provide 
approximately sixteen to twenty homes 
for local people experiencing or at risk of 
homelessness. Modular construction is 
a modern method of building, involving 
the construction of units off-site under 
controlled conditions and their assembly 
on-site. This approach ensures higher 
quality control, significant time savings 
and reduced environmental impact.
The proposed scheme will be procured 
through a suitable competition, with the 
final cost dependent on factors such as 
site value, location and utility availability. 
The project will comply with all relevant 
regulations and guidelines, ensuring a 
maximum lifespan with potential for 
adaptive reuse.
Next steps include site assessment and 
selection, finalising the project brief and 
confirming the procurement and delivery 
models. Innovative modular homeless 
housing proposals offer a promising and 
practical solution to the homelessness 
crisis. By leveraging modern construction 
techniques and sustainable design 
principles, these proposals can provide 
safe, dignified and adaptable housing for 
those in need.

Quality Housing
Clonburris SDZ: Proposed Non-Material Amendment to Planning Scheme
A proposed non-material amendment to 
the Clonburris Strategic Development 
Zone Planning Scheme was submitted to 
An Coimisiún Pleanála on 11 September 
this year by SDCC. 
This amendment is required to ensure 
that the planning scheme responds 
to national policy objectives and 
infrastructure planning, while remaining 
firmly within the overall vision for 
Clonburris.
The proposed changes reflect a carefully 
balanced and policy-aligned reallocation 
of residential units across the Strategic 
Development Zone. 
This improves the alignment of housing 
delivery with existing and planned 
infrastructure. Adjustments have been 
made in response to national policy 
changes, on-the-ground development 
activity, the delivery of key public 
infrastructure and updated site-specific 
constraints.
The proposed non-material amendment 
preserves the overall vision for Clonburris 
as a compact and sustainable community, 
while enabling continued progress 
in delivering housing, infrastructure 
and amenities across the Strategic 
Development Zone. 
There is currently no decision timeline 
from An Coimisiún Pleanála, but updates 
will be issued as they are received.
Planning permission has also been 
granted for the development of three 
major parks within the Clonburris 
Strategic Development Zone, marking 
a significant step in delivering high-
quality green infrastructure and new 
public open spaces for the area. The 
approved proposals are a key part of the 
Clonburris parks and green infrastructure 
strategy, ensuring that sports, play and 
biodiversity-focused spaces are provided 
as new homes are delivered. 
The first park, Griffeen Valley Park 
Extension, will cover approximately 15.9 
hectares and extend the existing park. 
It will include a senior all-weather GAA 
pitch that can be adapted for football, 
two natural grass pitches, tennis and 
padel courts, basketball facilities, 
allotments and two large destination play 
areas. Ecological measures will feature 
new attenuation ponds and significant 
biodiversity planting.
Grand Canal Park South, at around 17.3 
hectares, will transform an existing open 
space with two natural soccer pitches, 
play areas, allotments and reinforced tree 
planting along the canal corridor.
Na Cluainte Park South, covering about 
four hectares and located beside a 
proposed school site, will include an 
all-weather and a natural soccer pitch, 
basketball courts, multi-sports facilities, 
a large play area and ecological features 
such as ponds and varied topography. 
These parks have been designed in line 
with the approved Clonburris Parks and 
Landscape Strategy and the Clonburris 
Biodiversity Management Plan. Together, 
these plans ensure that the new parks will 
deliver high-quality recreation, enhance 
ecological value and integrate with 
sustainable drainage systems across the 
Strategic Development Zone.
The three parks are a core element of the 
Clonburris phasing strategy, ensuring that 
as housing is delivered, residents gain 
timely access to sports, play and natural 
amenity spaces.

THRIVE Funding for Rathfarnham Castle Stables and Courtyard
the project will also act as an exemplar 
conservation initiative, restoring the 
historic fabric of a protected structure that 
forms part of the curtilage of Rathfarnham 
Castle, an important national monument 
and visitor destination in the county.
With Part 8 approved for the development 
at the July council meeting, the awarding 
of €7 million through THRIVE funding 
represents a major vote of confidence in 
SDCC’s vision for the project. Engagement 
with local communities and their role in 
shaping the future of this project was a 
critical step in unlocking this opportunity 
and supporting the regeneration of 
Rathfarnham Stables and Courtyards.
Following the extensive public consultation 
process associated with the preparation 
of Part 8 for the development, the project 
has now entered the detailed design stage, 
A Thriving Economy
SDCC welcomes the announcement of 
€7 million in THRIVE funding to support 
the redevelopment of the historic 
Rathfarnham Stables and Courtyards, a 
flagship tourism initiative in the county. 
The funding is provided through the 
Government’s THRIVE scheme—Town 
Centre First Heritage Revival Scheme—co-
funded by the Government of Ireland and 
the European Union through the European 
Regional Development Fund Southern, 
Eastern and Midland Regional Programme 
2021–2027.
This landmark project will regenerate 
Rathfarnham Stables and Courtyards, 
incorporating four historic courtyards 
that will be brought back to life. The 
development will include a multi-purpose 
event space, arts and crafts areas, a new 
restaurant and café, outdoor event spaces 
and a new cultural facility. Acting as a 
key gateway for the village and county, 
the project will link Rathfarnham Village 
with Rathfarnham Park and Rathfarnham 
Castle, creating an important cultural, 
heritage and public amenity for visitors 
and the local community.
The reimagining of Rathfarnham 
Stables and Courtyards will have a 
transformational impact on the area, 
creating a mixed-use cultural, arts, 
tourism, hospitality and community 
development, complete with a network of 
public open spaces that will bring vibrancy 
and vitality to the village. In supporting 
job creation and the local economy, 
with all details to be finalised before 
construction begins in early next year. 
Building on the consultation process to 
date and ensuring continued engagement, 
a key part of the project will involve the 
redesign of the Sean Keating Garden, 
which will be carried out in consultation 
with the local community.
Rathfarnham Stables and Courtyards 
is a central part of the delivery of the 
county’s tourism strategy, and SDCC looks 
forward to working with the Department 
of Housing, Local Government and 
Heritage, the Southern Regional 
Assembly, the Office of Public Works, the 
local community and project partners, 
the McHugh Group, in delivering this 
initiative and supporting the economic 
development of the county.

From Zero to Demo in Two Weeks at Work IQ
A Thriving Economy
Work IQ recently hosted the Regional Demo 
Day for the National AI Hackathon, organised 
by TechIreland. With up to fifty people in 
attendance, teams of startups, students 
and corporate innovators had just two weeks 
to build practical AI solutions for a range 
of real-world challenges. The challenge 
placed a strong emphasis on people-centred 
and ethical AI development across several 
sectors.
The atmosphere was lively and engaging, as 
teams pitched their ideas, received feedback 
from expert judges—including previous 
winners, local entrepreneurs, technology 
executives and founders—and networked 
with fellow innovators. Work IQ’s flexible 
and collaborative space provided the ideal 
environment to celebrate creativity and 
entrepreneurship, highlighting the growing AI 
ecosystem in Ireland.
Five teams presented solutions focused 
on automating the marking of Leaving 
Certificate papers, retina-based access 
control for data, automation of ransomware 
detection, generative AI-driven dentist 
education and microlearning for the 
construction sector.
The winning team, LaunchLoop, went on 
to present their solution to automate the 
marking of Leaving Certificate papers—
currently a €56 million cost to the state—
at the National Showcase in Galway on 18 
September. Their approach was commended 
for its innovation and for embracing 
technology to address modern challenges.
South Dublin Business Showcase at National Ploughing Championships
Flaunta, a small business from Clondalkin, 
was supported by the Local Enterprise 
Office to exhibit to almost three hundred 
thousand people at the National Ploughing 
Championships in September. 
Founded by Angelina Sheridan and 
Hope Hayes, Flaunta designs bags and 
accessories that combine style with 
functionality and are made from vegan 
leather.
Flaunta was part of the Local Enterprise 
Village, which featured thirty small 
businesses from across Ireland. The Local 
Enterprise Village is an initiative of the 
Local Enterprise Offices, who partnered 
with Google this year to enhance the 
experience. 
Google hosted talks and demonstrations 
in the village, helping small businesses and 
entrepreneurs explore digital tools and 
artificial intelligence to grow their ideas. 
Earlier in the year, Flaunta featured at 
Showcase and won the Local Enterprise 
Award for Best Startup. 
The company also extended its reach on 
social media, achieving more than fifty 
million views for its products. Representing 
South Dublin at the National Ploughing 
Championships has capped an incredible 
year for Flaunta, as the business continues 
to go from strength to strength as a 
thriving company in the county.

Nature of Play Policy: Investing in Play, Inspiring Growth
Rathfarnham Castle Park Outdoor Classroom 
Funded through the Have Your Say 
Initiative, students from St. Mary’s B.N.S. 
recently joined Mayor of South Dublin, 
Cllr. Pamela Kearns and park rangers 
to explore the new outdoor classroom 
at Rathfarnham Castle Park. This quiet, 
sheltered space is designed to inspire 
outdoor learning, encourage curiosity and 
foster a stronger connection with nature. 
Outdoor learning offers many positive 
benefits, including improved focus, 
creativity, teamwork and wellbeing. It 
provides opportunities for hands-on 
discovery, sensory engagement and 
environmental awareness, helping children 
develop essential skills in a fun and active 
way. The new classroom will be a valuable 
community resource for years to come.
A Better Place
With a capital investment of more than 
€6 million, we are leading the way 
in delivering natural playspaces and 
an innovative teenspace programme 
across the county. These initiatives 
make play a vital part of public spaces, 
neighbourhoods and communities, 
supporting children and young people to 
be active, healthy and socially connected. 
The investment has expanded the 
network of public playgrounds to more 
than fifty and introduced new teenspaces, 
ensuring high-quality, accessible play 
opportunities for all.
Drawing on experience, community 
feedback and international best practice, 
we have developed The Nature of Play 
policy. This policy highlights the role 
of play in health, wellbeing, personal 
development and community cohesion. 
It provides examples of best practice 
and sets out how SDCC will continue 
to deliver high-quality play and outdoor 
recreation over the next five years.
These programmes and policies reflect 
our commitment to integrated, inclusive 
and safe communities. The provision of 
playspaces and teenspaces over the past 
decade, supported by more than €6 
million in capital investment, continues to 
strengthen the county as a place where 
children and young people can thrive.
Heritage Week Celebrates Local Roots
National Heritage Week took place 
between 16 and 24 August, with the 
theme of ‘Exploring our Foundation’. Our 
Heritage Week event list was co-ordinated 
by the Library Service, and funding for 
these activities was drawn annually from 
the County Heritage Plan budget.
A total of twenty-one events were 
organised for Heritage Week, including 
exhibitions, walks, tours, outdoor events, 
talks, workshops and children’s activities. 
In keeping with this year’s theme, 
genealogy and family history workshops 
proved popular, as did Viking and medieval 
armoury events.
In addition to council-funded and 
organised events, the Office of Public 
Works hosted activities in St. Enda’s 
Park and Rathfarnham Castle. Local 
communities and environmental groups 
across South Dublin County also held 
local history walks and music recitals, 
contributing to a vibrant and engaging 
Heritage Week for all

Little Library Brings Books to Tallaght Hospital
“The Little Library,” A new LibCabinet has 
been launched in partnership between 
SDCC Libraries and Library & Information 
Services at Tallaght University Hospital. 
Located in the hospitals foyer, the self-
service kiosk brings books and reading 
directly to patients, staff and visitors, 
making access to reading material easier 
for everyone in the hospital setting.
The LibCabinet allows users to borrow, 
return and browse a curated collection 
of books without needing to visit a library 
branch. By placing the kiosk in a busy area, 
the project offers relaxation, distraction 
and comfort to those who may be 
experiencing stressful times. Membership 
of the library is free, and once registered, 
members can use their card as they would 
in any branch. In addition to borrowing 
books, members can access eBooks, 
audiobooks and a wide range of digital 
resources.
For patients staying in hospital or 
visitors spending time with loved ones, 
the LibCabinet provides a way to stay 
connected with the outside world. For 
staff, it offers opportunities for rest and 
wellbeing during busy shifts. The location 
highlights the commitment of both 
organisations to supporting physical health 
and also mental and emotional wellbeing.
We hope the service will inspire further 
collaborations, showing how libraries can 
adapt and bring the pleasure of reading to 
new settings.
Connected Communities
County hall was the venue for the 
Moldovan parliamentary elections on 28 
September, providing Moldovan citizens 
living in South Dublin with the opportunity 
to vote locally. The polling station was 
organised in partnership with the Embassy 
of the Republic of Moldova, following a 
request to support the democratic process 
for the Moldovan community. National 
figures show that the Moldovan community 
in Ireland is growing, with most residents 
concentrated in Dublin and its surrounding 
areas. We continue to support the needs 
of all international communities, including 
Moldovan citizens. 
The foyer featured flag displays and 
a photo area decorated with flowers, 
reflecting the traditional style of 
Moldovan polling stations. Both the 
Irish and Moldovan flags were flown, 
and digital screens displayed election 
visuals throughout the day. Council staff 
worked with embassy representatives 
to ensure all arrangements met council 
requirements and provided a welcoming 
environment for voters. This collaboration 
with the Moldovan Embassy demonstrates 
our openness to facilitating democratic 
engagement for residents of South Dublin 
from diverse backgrounds.

Red Line Book Festival 2025: 
Fourteen Years of Stories, Creativity, and Community
The Red Line Book Festival returns from 
13 to 19 October, bringing a vibrant 
celebration of literature, creativity and 
community to the county. 
Now in its fourteenth year, the festival 
has become a hub for literature, art and 
connection, showcasing local talent, 
welcoming international guests and 
making culture accessible for everyone.
This year’s programme offers something 
for all ages. Families can enjoy the 
Curious Case of the Irish Yeti at Parthalán 
Place, while fans of the supernatural can 
join Ben Machell for discussions at the 
Civic Theatre. Politics enthusiasts will 
hear from Gavan Reilly on the secrets of 
Leinster House, and book lovers can meet 
authors including Helen Fielding, Roisín 
O’Donnell, Paul McVeigh and Booker 
Prize winner Paul Lynch. Local writers, 
such as first-time author Luke Devlin, will 
also feature, highlighting the festival’s 
support for emerging talent.
Art and illustration are central to the 
festival, with Celina Buckley as artist in 
residence. Her five-week workshop series 
will end with an exhibition at Ballyroan 
Library, and interactive Draw Along 
sessions for young artists will be led by 
Owen Churcher and Niamh Sharkey. 
Alan Nolan adds energy with his family 
show featuring Molly Malone and Bram 
Cultural Richness
Stoker.
Accessibility is a priority, with Irish Sign 
Language interpretation at selected 
events, sensory-friendly spaces for 
children with additional needs and buses 
from local libraries. Events will take place 
in venues including Rathfarnham Castle, 
Brú Chrónáin, Rathcoole Courthouse and 
Parthalán Place.
Whether discovering a new author, 
joining a workshop or enjoying the 
festival atmosphere, the Red Line Book 
Festival 2025 promises stories, surprises 
and inspiration for all. 
Full programme and booking details are 
available at redlinefestival.ie.

Mobile Library Rolls into the Ploughing Championships
Our mobile library service recently 
travelled to the National Ploughing 
Championships, joining the event at the 
invitation of the Department of Rural and 
Community Development, the Gaeltacht 
and Libraries Ireland. 
Over three days, the book-filled bus 
became a pop-up library, welcoming 
children, farmers and book lovers from 
across the country. Visitors browsed a 
wide selection of books, checked out 
titles and learned how easy it is to borrow 
and return books with the national 
library system, which makes every library 
accessible no matter where you live.
The National Ploughing Championships 
are known for celebrating agriculture, 
but they also highlight culture and 
community. 
The presence of the mobile library service 
helped sow the seeds of reading and 
demonstrated that library services can 
reach people wherever they are. Our 
staff were delighted to meet so many 
new readers and share information about 
library membership, which is free and 
open to all.
By bringing books directly to the fields, 
the mobile library service showed how 
libraries adapt to meet the needs of 
communities, supporting literacy and 
lifelong learning in every setting. 
Cultural Richness
Féile na Sléibhte Returns 
The Dublin Mountains Partnership (DMP) 
has been active for seventeen years, creating 
and maintaining the Dublin Mountains Way, 
supporting sustainable recreation, and 
encouraging environmental improvements.
Building on the success of the first Dublin 
Mountains Festival, Féile na Sléibhte, in 
2024, the DMP held the second festival 
in 2025 to celebrate and showcase this 
landscape. Running from 1 to 11 October, 
the programme featured talks, themed 
walks, a sheepdog demonstration, music, 
Irish language events, a community day, and 
workshops on sustainability, dog handling, 
and sharing nature with children. Highlights 
included National Tree Day at Tibradden 
Wood with three local schools and a dark 
skies talk at Glenasmole Community Centre.
For those who missed the festival, DMP 
hosts events throughout the year, including 
bat walks, guided hikes with volunteer 
rangers, and activities for Heritage Week, 
National Tree Day, and World Environment 
Day. Updates and bookings are available on 
the DMP website (www.dublinmountains.ie) 
or on Eventbrite.
DMP partners include SDCC, Coillte, Dublin 
City Council, Dún Laoghaire-Rathdown 
County Council, and the National Parks 
and Wildlife Service. The 2022–2026 
Strategic Plan sets out a vision of the 
Dublin Mountains as an area of outstanding 
beauty and sustainable recreation, where 
visitors can enjoy the hills, learn about 
their environment and culture, and respect 
local communities and other users. For 
further information on the Dublin Mountains 
Partnership and the Dublin Mountains 
Partnership Strategic Plan 2022–2026, 
contact info@dublinmountains.ie or 
communications@sdublincoco.ie.

Work Progresses on Local Community Safety Partnership in South Dublin
Rent Payments Made Simple Using “Quick Pay”
As part of our ongoing plan to use digital 
technology to make services easier and 
more accessible for customers, housing 
tenants can now pay their rent online using 
a credit or debit card. Tenants have the 
flexibility to pay at any time by using the 
“Pay for it” link on the SDCC website. This 
new service allows payments to be made 
on weekends and outside normal office 
hours, giving tenants greater convenience 
and control over their finances.
With the introduction of online payments, 
tenants no longer need to call the cash 
office to pay by phone. The system also 
enables tenants to make one-off lump 
sum payments, which can help reduce 
arrears more efficiently. This online 
payment service is available to tenants 
living in council, RAS and leased properties, 
ensuring that a wide range of residents can 
benefit from this improved service.
A new Local Community Safety Partnership 
(LCSP) is being established in South 
Dublin as part of a nationwide programme 
to rethink how safety and wellbeing are 
supported at community level. The LCSP 
will bring together residents, community 
groups, local authorities, An Garda 
Síochána and other key agencies to plan 
and work in partnership. Its purpose is 
to identify local safety concerns, agree 
practical solutions and build stronger 
connections between communities and the 
services that support them.
Unlike traditional policing forums, the 
LCSP will have a wider focus. It recognises 
that community safety goes beyond 
policing alone and also includes access to 
supports in areas such as youth services, 
health, education and social inclusion. By 
combining local knowledge with agency 
expertise, the LCSP aims to ensure safer, 
more connected and more resilient 
communities.
The partnership will provide an opportunity 
to address issues such as anti-social 
behaviour, substance misuse, youth 
supports, road safety and access to 
services, while also encouraging initiatives 
that strengthen community spirit.
In November, work will focus on finalising 
the structure of the partnership and inviting 
representation from across the community 
and relevant agencies. Further information 
will be shared as planning progresses.
People First
Our Housing Customer Centre – Here to Help You
The Housing Customer Centre, located in 
County Hall, is a modern and comfortable 
space designed to make things easy for 
customers. At the centre, visitors can collect 
and submit forms for social housing, rent, 
grants and other services. Staff are available 
to assist with maintenance requests and 
rent account queries, providing guidance 
on digital services and support with online 
applications. Customers can also make 
appointments to access information and 
support for allocations, HAP, homeless 
services, housing grants and estate 
management queries.
We are currently developing clear guidance 
for staff, robust procedures for managing 
appointments and ongoing training to 
ensure every customer receives the highest 
standard of care.

Art, Performance and Community Spirit Light Up Culture Night
From the lively streets of Parthalán Place 
to the historic grounds of Lucan House, 
audiences enjoyed an evening filled with 
music, theatre, dance and immersive 
experiences. Packed venues, innovative 
performances and welcoming spaces 
allowed everyone to celebrate together, 
highlighting the richness of the cultural 
scene and the power of the arts to 
connect people.
In Parthalán Place, Tallaght, festivities 
began early on Friday, 19 September, 
with Tallaght Library hosting a family-
friendly programme. Children and parents 
enjoyed Classical Kids, an interactive 
concert introducing young audiences 
to live music, followed by laughter and 
amazement during The Magic Show with 
Murf the Magician. 
These daytime events set the stage for an 
evening where creativity took over local 
cultural landmarks.
That night, Rua Red and Parthalán Place 
became the centre of SPECTRUM, a 
cross-disciplinary series co-produced 
by Rua Red, SoFFt Productions and 
the SDCC Arts Office’s youth music 
programme, NOISE Music. Part of 
the national Culture Night Late 
strand, SPECTRUM featured roaming 
performances, immersive sound zones 
and a sense of spontaneity. 
Rua Red’s Gallery 1 was transformed into 
a live venue, showcasing music collectives 
BPM, Tallaght’s Burner Records and 
young DJs from the NOISE DJ Collective. 
Creative Places MacUillium musicians, 
poet Sandisiwe Khupe and the Afro Vibes 
dance collective added their unique 
voices.
Striking visuals, projected artworks and 
a laser show by Robin Price elevated 
the performances. Outside, Parthalán 
Place hosted a block party-style 
celebration with live graffiti, hip-hop 
and contemporary dance. The SoFFt 
Space offered a neurodivergent-friendly 
environment, providing calm and 
accessibility.
Elsewhere, Lucan House welcomed five 
hundred attendees for a night of music, 
storytelling and celebration curated by 
Artscope. Highlights included a flash mob 
by The Rubik’s Ensemble, an immersive 
sound installation from Abigail Smith and 
a debut performance by a new trio of Irish 
musicians. The headline act, Nightvisiting, 
led by Lisa Lambe, blended storytelling 
and song.
With children’s entertainment, 
refreshments and a family-friendly 
atmosphere, Lucan House captured the 
heart of the community. As one attendee 
said, “I came for the music, but I stayed 
for the atmosphere.”
From experimental performances to 
intergenerational gatherings, Culture 
Night 2025 showcased the county’s 
artistic vibrancy, transforming familiar 
spaces into cultural landmarks and 
bringing art and community together for 
one unforgettable night.
County Matters

Communicating Climate Action: New Climate Action Website and Story-
map Launched
Climate leadership is a key objective for 
SDCC and is reflected in our Corporate 
Plan. Aiming for a low-carbon and climate-
resilient county, the Climate Action Plan 
influences the work of most council 
services. Whether it is Ireland’s first publicly 
owned district heating network in Tallaght 
or the extensive and growing active travel 
network, we aim to demonstrate climate 
leadership at a local level.
In protecting property and infrastructure 
from flooding through three flood 
alleviation schemes, and in supporting 
nature and biodiversity by expanding 
the green infrastructure network, we are 
working to establish sustained climate 
action across South Dublin County.
Alongside this work, it is equally important 
to communicate clearly what is being done 
and why, and to engage with residents and 
the wider community. To support this, we 
are launching an innovative, interactive 
climate action StoryMap on the newly 
revamped Climate Action website. The new 
website and StoryMap will be launched to 
the public in October.
The map will showcase climate actions, 
projects and community partnerships. 
These interactive maps will be accessible 
to all, allowing the public to view our 
work in their areas in an engaging way. 
The StoryMap will also highlight the 
groundswell of community-led action that 
is building across the county.
Some highlights featured on the Climate 
Action StoryMap include the work of the 
public lighting retrofit team, who are 
updating our largest energy user to light-
emitting diode (LED) lights, significantly 
reducing electricity use. 
Details are also provided on upcoming 
energy projects to help decarbonise key 
buildings, as well as an innovative solar 
power project at Arthurstown Landfill. The 
rollout of sustainable drainage systems is 
outlined, as is the continued transition of 
fleet vehicles away from fossil fuels.
The StoryMap also shows the location of 
our mini woodlands and natural meadows, 
delivered by the public realm team in 
collaboration with dedicated community 
groups. Other features include climate 
action measures incorporated by the 
transport department in the delivery of 
the Rosemount District Enhancement 
project, and a project on building homes 
sustainably, led by the architect’s 
department. Ongoing climate action 
engagement through annual events such 
as Dublin Climate Action Week is also 
highlighted.
The StoryMap is part of the dedicated 
climate action website for South Dublin, 
www.southdublinclimate.ie, where updates 
on progress are regularly hosted. The 
focus is to inform and inspire, reinforcing 
the necessity of climate action across the 
county.

Halloween in South Dublin
This year, to raise awareness and encourage 
everyone to stay safe, a colourful 
information leaflet will be published with 
facts and tips on how to enjoy Halloween 
safely. The leaflet also includes details 
about family events taking place in 
libraries across the county. Information is 
available on incentives designed to protect 
community open spaces from damage 
caused by illegal bonfires. 
“Bulbs Not Bonfires” is a reward available 
through the innovative Social Credits 
Scheme, offering communities spring 
flowers in return for organising alternative 
Halloween activities that protect the 
environment. Every Social Credit applicant 
or group will receive a free pass to 
Ballymount Civic Amenity Centre from 22 
October, making it easier to recycle. Each 
pass allows one car entry and is valid until 
28 November this year.
Step into the shadows this Samhain and join 
in for some frightful fun at Tallaween on 31 
October and Spookdalkin on 2 November. 
Enjoy creepy cinema screenings, zombie 
entertainment, fire performers, food 
trucks and more. Prizes will be awarded for 
the most spooktacular costumes. SDCC 
Libraries are celebrating Halloween in style 
this October with a packed programme of 
events for all ages. From costume swaps 
and storytimes to science workshops, 
family films and creative crafts, there is 
plenty to keep children, teens and adults 
entertained. 
The festivities begin early with Halloween 
costume swaps across library branches, 
giving families the chance to trade last 
year’s outfits for something new. Tallaght 
Library launches its big Halloween day 
on 11 October with a costume swap, 
a chance to meet Spiderman, a silent 
disco for children aged three and up, and 
an afternoon Family Fun Day featuring 
jugglers, balloon animals and face painting. 
Lucan Library will also host a swap on 9 
October at 6pm, with costume drop-offs 
starting from 6 October. 
Throughout the month, families can enjoy 
spooky storytimes and craft sessions at 
Clondalkin, Tallaght, North Clondalkin and 
Lucan Library. Makers of all ages can get 
creative with trick-or-treat bag workshops, 
colourful art sessions and teen costume-
making. Science fans in Ballyroan Library 
will enjoy Erupting Pumpkins!, a hands-on 
workshop on 30 October where children 
aged nine and over can make a pumpkin 
model and watch it erupt. Adults can join 
the Creative Spirits Tote Bag Workshop on 
21 October to design a custom Halloween 
bag. 
Halloween week will be especially busy. 
Lucan Library hosts 3D printing for children 
aged nine and over at noon on 30 October, 
followed by two lively performances of the 
Viking Show with Knights for Hire at 2pm 
and 3pm. Later that afternoon, children 
aged nine to twelve can join Halloween Art 
and Creativity at 3.30pm. 
On 31 October, Lucan rounds off its 
programme with a Card Swap for Kids at 
2.30pm, while Clondalkin Library will be 
buzzing all day with a scavenger hunt and 
drop-in crafts. 
Music and movies add to the fun, with 
North Clondalkin’s Halloween Disco at 
NCHell on 24 October, film screenings 
in Tallaght and North Clondalkin on 29 
October, and a special big-screen showing 
of Hotel Transylvania. Younger children 
are catered for as well, with Tallaght’s 
Halloween Toddler Time with Twinkle Kids 
on 31 October, featuring gentle stories, 
music and movement.

Muintir Chrónáin & SDCC pay tribute to President Higgins in Clondalkin
SDCC were proud to support a very special 
tribute to the President of Ireland, Mícheál 
D. Higgins and his wife Sabina in Áras 
Chrónáin, Clondalkin on 4 October. 
The event was organised by Muintir 
Chrónáin to express gratitude to the 
President for all his work to promote Irish 
language, heritage and the arts during his 
time as President of Ireland and indeed 
throughout his career.
Mayor Pamela Kearns and representatives 
of Muintir Chrónáin welcomed the 
President upon arrival before Muintir 
Chrónáin chairperson Meadhbh Ní 
Cheallaigh spoke about the challenge 
President Higgins presented in 1993, in his 
then tole as Minister for Arts, Culture and 
the Gaeltacht, for Clondalkin to “have a 
Gaeltacht of their own, the first Gaeltacht 
in the capital’ which inspired the work 
of Muintir Chrónáin in achieving  ‘Líonra 
Gaeilge’ official Irish language network 
status for Clondalkin in 2021.
During the event which was attended by 
councillors from both SDCC’s Corporate 
Policy Group and the Clondalkin, 
Newcastle, Rathcoole, Saggart and Brittas 
Area Committee, local poet Barry Currivan 
read a poem he had written especially for 
the occasion ‘Of Stars, Of Dust, Of Grit’ 
and this was followed by Edel Ní Arrachtáin 
singing ‘The Tricoloured Ribbon’.  
Then there was a performance from by 
the band KILA who performed tracks 
from ‘Ómós’, their specially commissioned 
Mícheál D. Higgins tribute album, a copy of 
which was presented to the President on 
the night.
There is no doubt that President Higgins 
thoroughly enjoyed the event which was a 
source of pride for the President and his 
family, for Muintir Chrónáin, Áras Chrónáin, 
the community of Clondalkin, South Dublin 
County Council and for everyone who was 
present. Go raibh míle maith agat agus 
buíochas mór to everyone involved in the 
organisation and presentation of the event.
